repositories.role: Scrape, crawl, map and extraction platform; optional Rust Firecrawl Local executable.
verifiedCapabilities: Local scrape/crawl/map and Firecrawl v2 localhost API
Static HTTP with optional Chrome rendering
Local PDF and Office parsing
Shared native HTML cleaning code
repositories.adoption: Evaluate the native Local adapter for Athena/document acquisition and compatible Rust workers, retaining the host's durable queue, exact identities, complete results and provenance.
limits: Local jobs live in memory and expire one hour after starting
Default local crawl limit is 100; do not mistake this for exhaustive completion
Local skips JSON and summary formats with warnings and ignores browser actions
Blocked local single-page requests may fall back to cloud; FIRECRAWL_CLOUD=off explicitly disables cloud handoff
No benchmark here establishes performance in our hosts

repositories.role: Async Python web extraction and browser orchestration.
verifiedCapabilities: CSS, XPath and regex extraction without an LLM
Markdown with headings, links, tables and citation references
Reusable sessions and browser pooling
Cached responses and memory-adaptive arun_many dispatcher
BFS, DFS, best-first traversal and resume state
Media, srcset, iframe and metadata extraction
repositories.adoption: Candidate Athena extraction worker using deterministic schemas, pooled browser resources and complete recorded responses. Preserve original HTML alongside parsed results.
limits: AdaptiveCrawler may stop when it judges a query answered; this is unsuitable as the completion condition for exhaustive catalogs
Hosted cloud and local library have different setup and cost models
Current source describes v0.9.6 dated 2026-11-20; do not assume older APIs
Do not adopt source performance claims as measured host results

verifiedCapabilities: Current 1.0.8 architecture runs Python against raw CDP in a persistent REPL using Pydantic AI
Supports explicit local browser selection
Agent output can be used to discover repeatable extraction steps
repositories.adoption: Optional final escalation for extraction requiring actual interactions. Turn repeatable routes into deterministic adapters once understood.
limits: Current browser and model defaults are cloud-backed
Version pinning is needed because the 1.x interface differs materially from older examples
Agent planning is not the default low-latency path for metadata, RSS or simple HTTP catalogs
No feedback or telemetry message was sent during this review

repositories.role: TypeScript crawler orchestration across HTTP and browser transports.
verifiedCapabilities: Persistent request queues
Configurable retries, session lifecycle and storage
AutoscaledPool considers CPU, memory and event-loop pressure
Experimental AdaptivePlaywrightCrawler can switch to HTTP-only extraction
repositories.adoption: Reuse queue/transport/parser separation and resource-aware scheduling in compatible Node/TypeScript workers. Keep all discovered work queued while controlling simultaneous work.
limits: AdaptivePlaywrightCrawler is explicitly experimental and constrains its handler interface
Concurrency limits must not become catalog/result limits
Old guessed source path packages/core/src/autoscaling/autoscaled_pool.ts returned 404; authoritative API documentation was used instead

repositories.role: Python request scheduling, middleware, extraction and resumable crawls.
verifiedCapabilities: JOBDIR persists queued/seen requests and spider state
Per-slot AutoThrottle derives target delay from observed latency and target concurrency
Throttle decreases are smoothed and increases are immediate
Fast non-200 responses cannot reduce throttle delay
repositories.adoption: Transfer per-origin fairness, retry classification, durable request state and error-aware delay behavior to host acquisition layers without introducing an unnecessary replacement framework.
limits: A JOBDIR is owned by one run and must not be shared between spiders/jobs
Documented resume uses clean shutdown
JavaScript rendering remains a separate transport concern

verifiedCapabilities: HTML, PDF, Office, text formats and other converters
Optional per-format dependency groups and plugins
Injected requests_session support
convert_stream accepts already fetched content
repositories.adoption: Use Athena's validated fetch path once, preserve original bytes and metadata, then dispatch conversion by content type. Supply seekable spooled streams for large inputs.
limits: convert_response collects the body in BytesIO
convert_stream buffers an entire nonseekable stream
Markdown is not a high-fidelity source-artifact replacement
Image captioning and speech transcription can depend on hosted services
It is not crawl orchestration

repositories.role: HTTP/browser sessions, parser and crawling framework.
verifiedCapabilities: Async fetchers and persistent sessions
CSS/XPath and similarity-based element relocation
Streaming spider output and pause/resume
Per-domain throttling with Retry-After
Recorded-response development replay
Existing-response parser integration with Scrapy
repositories.adoption: Candidate parsing/adapter layer for changing markup, with fixture replay and validation of recovered fields. Reuse already fetched responses.
limits: A similarity match is not proof of field identity or correctness
Preserve required fields, pagination and type checks before accepting selector recovery
Upstream universal access/bypass marketing was not verified and is not an acceptance claim

repositories.role: Android screen mirroring and input control.
verifiedCapabilities: USB/TCP-IP device screen/control
Audio forwarding and recording
Virtual display and physical input simulation
repositories.adoption: Keep separate for an explicitly requested Android-only extraction workflow. Do not add it to ordinary web acquisition dependencies.
limits: Not a web crawler, HTML parser or structured extraction engine
Requires an Android device and applicable device permissions

verifiedCapabilities: Build reusable rules from requested sample values
Supply existing HTML instead of fetching
Save/load learned rules as JSON
Exact/similar result modes
repositories.adoption: Use as adapter-authoring assistance with pre-fetched HTML and multiple recorded page variants. Keep the host's network/cancellation/error policies.
limits: Source _fetch_html uses direct requests.get with no default timeout/status check
request_args.pop('headers') mutates the caller's dictionary
Learned rules rely on class/style attributes and structural/positional traversal
No-maintenance claims are not justified

repositories.role: Browser-compatible TLS/HTTP handshakes through modified curl/libcurl.
verifiedCapabilities: Browser TLS extension and cipher configuration
HTTP/2 handshake configuration
CLI and libcurl integration
repositories.adoption: Keep transport compatibility optional behind the host acquisition contract. Compare maintained descendants such as lexiforest/curl_cffi before selecting a package.
limits: Inspected original profile table includes Chrome 116/Firefox 117 and older profiles
Does not execute application JavaScript
Handshake emulation is not every browser behavior and does not guarantee access

zeroLossChecks: Control simultaneous work, not result quantity
Distinguish terminal pagination from configured limits
Coalesce only identical request identity and preserve independent consumers
Never let fast errors increase request rate
Use deterministic field validation and replay fixtures
Fetch once and parse existing complete content
Keep source files and rich original metadata alongside Markdown
implementationGuidance.evidenceBoundary: All adoption recommendations are engineering judgments informed by source inspection. No upstream marketing performance number is presented as a benchmark in Athena or its consumer repositories. Individual consumer changes require their own equivalent-work runtime tests.
